articles.title: Why House Republicans are pulling their $5 million from a key N.Y. battleground seat
articles.author: Andrew Solender
articles.summary: House Republicans are effectively abandoning what was supposed to be a key battleground district in New York over concerns that their candidate, state Sen. Peter Oberacker, is too flawed to seriously compete, sources tell Axios. Why it matters: Expect to see more of this cold calculus as the general election heats up, with both parties determining where their money will actually make enough of a difference to be worth spending. In this case, the GOP has determined that New York's 19th district, a perennial battleground seat that has routinely changed hands between Democrats and Republicans over the last several election cycles, doesn't warrant the investment. The seat, currently held by freshman Rep. Josh Riley (D-N.Y.), was one of the National Republican Congressional Committee's stated targets as recently as last month . Driving the news: Congressional Leadership Fund, House Republicans' main super PAC, removed all its money in the district last week, according to ad tracking firm AdImpact.
